section_new.excerpt: # Retries and backpressure **Question.** When do retries absorb transient failure, and when do they amplify overload? **Short answer.** A retry helps only when the failure is transient and the retry budget is bounded. Without a budget, backoff and jitter, retries add load to an already saturated system. Backpressure, queue capacity and a bulkhead decide whether the system rejects work explicitly or collapses under it

It combines stock-and-flow reasoning, discrete-event simulation, Monte Carlo uncertainty, comparative decision records and staged modernization-path simulation. section_new.heading: Purpose and mission

section_new.excerpt: ## The basic quantities - Arrival rate (lambda): requests per second offered to the queue. - Service capacity (mu): requests per second the server pool can complete when busy. - Utilization (rho): offered load divided by capacity, rho = lambda / mu for one server class, or lambda / (c * mu) for c identical servers. - Queue length: requests waiting for a server. - In-system count: waiting plus in service. - Time in sy
section_new.heading: The basic quantities

section_new.excerpt: ## Failure modes - **Hash drift.** A model or scenario is edited without regenerating its run. - **Unrecorded seed.** The result cannot be reproduced. - **Mutable dependency.** A library update changes the output and is not recorded. - **Timestamp-only provenance.** A file says when it was created but not what it used. - **Replay theater.** The command reruns the model but compares only the metric names, not the valu
section_new.heading: Failure modes

section_new.excerpt: ## Where the model fails - **Unit collapse.** A stock and a flow share a label. The model becomes dimensionally meaningless. - **Hidden stock.** Work waiting in a database, a client retry buffer or an operator queue is omitted. The visible backlog looks stable while total work grows elsewhere. - **Unbounded flow.** A service rate is treated as infinite because the server is "fast". The backlog then drains at an impos
section_new.heading: Where the model fails

section_new.heading: Required fields

section_new.heading: Failure modes

section_new.excerpt: ## Standard error For n independent replications with sample standard deviation s, the standard error of the mean is: se = s / sqrt(n) A 95% confidence interval under a normal approximation is: mean +/- 1.96 * se The interval is narrower when n is larger or the output is less variable. It does not become more valid if the replications are correlated or the output distribution is heavy-tailed. V12 uses the normal appr
section_new.heading: Standard error

section_new.heading: A worked cross-chapter synthesis

section_new.excerpt: ## From decision to boundary A model boundary is the line between the model's state and the rest of the world. It is not the same as a service boundary or a team boundary. section_new.heading: From decision to boundary

section_new.excerpt: ## Backpressure Backpressure is the explicit refusal or delay of work when capacity is exhausted. V12 uses three limits: - queue capacity: maximum waiting requests; - bulkhead: maximum waiting plus in-service requests; - timeout: maximum time an attempt may occupy the system. When a limit is reached, the request is rejected and counted. A model with an unbounded queue never rejects; it accumulates backlog and reports
section_new.heading: Backpressure

section_new.excerpt: ## Batch means and dependence Replications are independent by construction in V12: each replication uses its own seed. Within a replication, events are dependent by design. If a metric were computed from a single long run, batch means would be needed to estimate its standard error. section_new.heading: Failure modes

section_new.heading: The basic quantities
